hypotheses.content: m118's measured high-loading 1/1 completion is much later than its matched 2/1 and pure-EA completion. This does not support a uniform completion correction across its strong-solvent rows. Whether pure-EA completion remains early across loading is unresolved.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The largest recent completion failure had an accurate onset prediction. Boundary labels at two additional loadings test the scope of the failure and discourage a shared shift of both endpoints or all methoxy-carbonyl rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do 50- and 100-uL pure-EA measurements also finish near 8-9 mL, or does late completion appear at another loading? These labels will not establish reproducibility of the unusual 1/1 record itself.

hypotheses.content: For m115, observed pure-EA completion has a middle-loading maximum: 8.654, 17.329 and 12.258 mL at 50, 100 and 150 uL. At 1/1, completion instead changes from 16.700 to approximately 18.04-18.08 mL. Reproducibility of the pure-EA maximum remains unknown.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A repeat at the discrepant midpoint can distinguish a reproducible solvent-loading association from record variation. That distinction affects both the conditional target mean and how much weight retraining should place on an apparent local feature.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does another 100-uL pure-EA measurement remain near 17.3 mL completion, approach the current 12.5-mL forecast, or show substantial same-condition dispersion?

hypotheses.content: m4's high-loading completion increase extends across measured 5/1, 10/1 and 20/1, rejecting the previous proposed maximum at 10/1. At matched 5/1 and 20/1, high loading advances onset by about 1.1 mL while delaying completion by about 5.8 mL. Its extent into 2/1 and 1/1 remains unmeasured.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The stronger-eluent extension tests whether retraining has learned a solvent-dependent completion-loading association or only a correction near the acquired weak-solvent rows. Opposite onset and completion movements require endpoint-specific learning.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 150 uL, do 2/1 and 1/1 finish close to their measured 50-uL counterparts as forecast, or does a substantial completion increase persist?

hypotheses.content: m138's later 2/1 endpoints relative to 1/1 are observed at both 50 and 150 uL. The current lower-loading 5/1 forecast places completion earlier than both measured strong-solvent values, proposing a localized 2/1 enhancement whose weaker-eluent side is unestablished.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A matched 5/1 label determines whether the repaired 2/1 response is localized or extends toward weaker eluent. It adds a direct condition-response constraint in a compound without hydrogen-bond donors or acceptors.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 50 uL, does 5/1 completion fall below the measured 13.975-mL 2/1 value, as the 9.318-mL forecast proposes?

hypotheses.content: m127 has a measured pure-EA completion increase of 2.575 mL relative to 1/1 at 150 uL. The predictor proposes a similar increase at 50 uL, but neither lower-loading endpoint pair has been measured. Transfer across loading is therefore unresolved.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Completing four matched corners tests whether a boundary completion increase is reproducible across loading and whether it can occur without delaying onset. It also constrains positional-isomer transfer without assuming m115 and m127 share a correction.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 50 uL, is pure-EA completion later than 1/1 by roughly 2.6 mL, and does onset remain similar or advance?

hypotheses.content: m3's recent 50-uL 10/1 observation has later endpoints than its measured 100-uL 20/1 and 5/1 records, but those unmatched comparisons do not establish a nonmonotonic solvent segment. The current forecasts propose the 10/1-to-20/1 advance at both 50 and 100 uL.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The two missing crossed conditions separate solvent response from loading transfer after a recent two-endpoint underestimate. They test whether a newly learned local feature generalizes within a highly aromatic scaffold.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do matched 10/1 and 20/1 measurements show earlier onset and completion at 20/1 at both loadings, or was the apparent response caused by comparing different loadings?

feedback_interpretation:
The largest new selected failure was m118 at high-loading 1/1: completion was 41.550 mL, a 25.33-mL acquisition-time underestimate, while onset was accurate. Its measured 2/1 and pure-EA completion values are much earlier. I treat this as a condition-specific observation requiring scope testing, not evidence for a family-wide correction. The eligible pure-EA loading extensions test boundary transfer but cannot resolve reproducibility of the 1/1 record.
For m115, low-loading pure EA finished at only 8.654 mL. This rejects a simple low-versus-high loading interpretation of the previous discrepancy and identifies an observed middle-loading maximum. The corresponding 1/1 completion values vary much less. I now prioritize one repeat of the unusual pure-EA midpoint. Same-tuple dispersion elsewhere, including m92 records f7d6c68ef2b3f637bd05 and f6650af9162e038d4108, cautions against treating every isolated loading feature as deterministic.
The m4 pair rejected H73's proposed 10/1 maximum: high-loading completion increased from 20.883 through 22.592 to 23.550 mL across 5/1, 10/1 and 20/1. Both new completions remained underestimated at acquisition. Matched low-loading observations reveal a similar approximately 5.8-mL completion increase at 5/1 and 20/1, motivating stronger-eluent tests of its extent. The m138 outcomes instead supported the predicted 2/1-to-1/1 advance at both loadings, with modest loading differences. Its next useful question is the unmeasured weaker-eluent side.
For m69, 100-uL onset was still early at 20/1, locating its late-onset change closer to 50/1. Increasing loading at 50/1 advanced onset by 4.475 mL while completion increased by 1.567 mL. This strengthens endpoint-specific conditional loading evidence, but the current round can address other uncovered relationships. Quinoline's high-loading 1/1 onset closely matched its forecast and advanced only 0.567 mL relative to low loading, limiting transfer of its larger 2/1 loading association; completion was underestimated by 1.94 mL.
The m202 pure-EA label preserved endpoint ordering and rejected the predicted interval collapse. The m27 pure-EA label rejected H77's boundary rebound. m87 completion continued to decrease toward pure EA, weakening a general methoxy-carbonyl boundary-tail hypothesis. m127 did show a pure-EA completion increase, although smaller than forecast, making its lower-loading matched pair informative. The m55 measurements support a smooth intermediate solvent curve, so I defer further labels there. Separately identified recent CW feedback for m3 exposed underestimates of both 10/1 endpoints and motivates the crossed solvent-loading comparison. All errors discussed here are historical acquisition-time errors, not current-model residuals.
batch_rationale:
The batch turns recent failures into comparisons that can distinguish competing explanations. The m115 repeat addresses reproducibility before assigning a nonlinear loading rule. The m118 boundary pair tests whether its exceptional 1/1 completion has broader strong-solvent scope. The m127 pair completes a measured-reference solvent-loading experiment, while the m4 pair locates the stronger-eluent limit of an observed completion-loading association. The m138 point tests a specific predicted solvent reversal. Two m3 labels complete crossed conditions around a new CW failure, separating solvent shape from loading differences.
Other selections broaden the relationships learned. The m203 and m198 pairs measure missing strong-solvent segments in a hindered tertiary alcohol and a nitro aldehyde, testing completion plateaus and independent onset movement. m164 supplies intermediate coverage in an extended conjugated ketone. The m168 label isolates a recorded loading-solvent-volume contrast against a measured reference. These additions complement pending coverage of simple hydrocarbons, acrylates and halogenated ethers.
Expected value comes from learning the extent and transferability of structure-condition relationships across remaining rows. Large retention values and large elution intervals are not acquisition objectives. The single intentional repeated tuple has a concrete variance-versus-response question; the other supplements add distinct condition tuples. Quantile spans and CW distances are contextual model signals, and crossed quantiles are not calibrated epistemic uncertainty. Unrecorded experimental variation limits causal interpretation of all observed associations. The supplied 16 pending experiments and these 16 supplements, including their premeasurement predictions, are fixed before any new label reveal.
